subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Launch and diagnostic: personal artistic questions
essential_question: How can understanding artistic voice and advanced composition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Activate prior knowledge about personal artistic questions, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of personal artistic questions.
Check, revise, or improve work about personal artistic questions using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about personal artistic questions.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 1 of "Artistic Voice and Advanced Composition" (unit 1, grade 8) is a diagnostic probe on personal artistic questions. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Develop a coherent visual series with an artist statement and process evidence. Today's work contributes to that by handling personal artistic questions at the launch and diagnostic stage, against the unit's wider topics of personal artistic questions, composition and visual hierarchy, symbol metaphor and abstraction, and style studies without copying. This session is formative: it is scored on completeness and honesty of the record, not on getting a polished result.
primary_task: Before any instruction on personal artistic questions, make a short baseline response so you can see your own starting point later. Spend a few minutes producing something — a quick sketch, a short pattern, a few bars, a rough plan, or a written description if you prefer not to produce a piece today. Then write three things you already notice about personal artistic questions and one question you cannot yet answer. Keep this baseline; you will compare later work against it. Nothing here is judged for quality, only for being honest and complete. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about personal artistic questions, and it belongs to "Artistic Voice and Advanced Composition", which also covers separate topics such as composition and visual hierarchy. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about personal artistic questions; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 8 the bar is independent work that anticipates the obvious objection: name the case most likely to break your result, test it, and report what happened.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task about personal artistic questions., The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
Address the lesson objective: Activate prior knowledge about personal artistic questions, surface initial thinking without penalty, and establish the unit question.
Produce the deliverable for a diagnostic probe: Dated baseline response (made or described in writing), three noticings, and one open question, preserved for later comparison.
Show the process, not only the result — a working log, draft, or annotated study.
Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: Dated baseline response (made or described in writing), three noticings, and one open question, preserved for later comparison.
critique_criteria: A dated baseline response to personal artistic questions exists and was made before any instruction.
Three specific noticings and one open question are recorded in writing.
The baseline is preserved for later comparison rather than discarded or overwritten.
A written description was accepted in place of a made piece if the student preferred; nothing required a camera, recording, or audience.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting personal artistic questions.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for personal artistic questions follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for personal artistic questions, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for personal artistic questions works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of personal artistic questions, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking personal artistic questions mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply personal artistic questions under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on personal artistic questions rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
